target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of pith (PO_0006109; PO lists medulla as a synonym)
reason: Cells of the central tissue of a moss stem seen in cross-section ('medulla cells loose, hyaline, in 12-20 rows'). Narrower: a cell of the pith. No pith cell class exists, so the bearer is a plant cell that is part of the pith.
Exact: the modified leaves around the moss antheridia are what the Plant Ontology calls perigonial bracts.
'scale' on its own was rejected as a generic part in the previous review. A lobe of an unnamed scale has the same problem: the organ that bears it (bract, hair, ligule, perianth scale) is missing.
Ambiguous. It can be an apical beak of a fruit, a leftover style base, a central column or a stump left on a stem ('leaving a small peg'). It cannot be placed without the organ.
Narrower: the persistent leaf-like plates of the protonema in Tetraphis and its relatives. It is a form of the protonema found in one small group of mosses, so a rule fits better than a new class.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part of labellum lobe (FLOPO_0986028); outside Orchidaceae: apex of corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006) part of corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017)
reason: Apex region of a lobe of the lip, expressed with the apex region pattern. 'Lip' is the orchid labellum in most of these statements; the plant family decides between labellum lobe and a lobe of the corolla lip.

A wart-like outgrowth with no organ named, the same problem as 'rib' and 'scale' in the previous review. Warts on a named organ are better recorded as that organ with the quality warty (PATO:0001361).

label: style head
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0009074 style
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is the enlarged distal portion of the style or styles (PO:0009074), bearing or surrounding the receptive stigmatic surfaces and, in Apocynaceae, joined to the anthers in the gynostegium. NOTE: No style head in PO; distinct from stigma PO:0009073. Propose to PO upstream.
reason: 'Pistil head' is the word some floras use for the style head of Apocynaceae (conical, fleshy, 1-1.5 mm). It is the same structure as 'stylehead' (item 27) and it occurs in several floras. Neither stigma nor style is right for it.
A phrase fragment that gives the unit of a count ('1-2 at each node'). The counted part comes before it; the stem node (PO_0020141) is only the place where it is counted.

Ambiguous between a disc-shaped fused androecium (synandrium FLOPO_0986014, e.g. Myristicaceae) and a floral disc next to the stamens (FLOPO_0986025). The hairy and hirsute statements fit both. It needs the family to decide.
Narrower or exact: the sheathing base of the leaf of palms and aroids (marcescent, membranous margins, 1.5-13 cm long) is a leaf sheath.

target: plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) part of peristome (PO_0030042)
reason: The basal membrane of the inner peristome is the low, joined base of the peristome; the examples say 'basal membrane'. It is expressed as the base region of the peristome.
A fragment: the second term of a ratio ('neck 1/2-1 times urn length', pattern 10). The part it refers to is the urn, sporangium theca (PO_0030041), and length is the quality.
French '-flore(s)' = '-flowered' in counts ('glomérules 3-7-flores'). It is a count of flowers per unit (pattern 03), so it belongs with the counted parts in flora_counted_parts.tsv.
Narrower: the axis or axes of a panicle inflorescence (PO_0030123). When a statement clearly means only the main rachis, first order inflorescence axis (PO_0025104) is better.
Narrower: veins running lengthwise in leaves, glumes and bracts; 'nerve' already maps to vascular bundle (rule C153). These statements are counts of veins.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part of spikelet rachilla (PO_0009080)
reason: The sterile prolongation of the grass spikelet rachilla beyond the uppermost floret. Its length and hairs belong to this distal part, not to the whole rachilla.

Narrower: the expanded distal part of a sheathing or leaf-like bract, as in Cyperaceae and Poaceae involucral bracts. The Plant Ontology has bract apex, base and margin but no bract lamina, so the bract is the nearest bearer.
A fragment that gives the unit of a count ('12-18 per row'); the counted part comes before it.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of leaf base (PO_0020040; PO lists 'leaf sheath base' and 'phyllid base' as synonyms)
reason: Cells of the sheathing base of a moss leaf (linear at the margin, short-rectangular in the middle). Leaf sheath (PO_0020104) belongs to the leaves of flowering plants, so the moss leaf base is the safer whole.
A quality. The part follows it ('persistent styles', 'persistent sheath').
Exact in use: reduced, sterile stamens counted in unisexual flowers are staminodes.
The margin of a stipule. The Plant Ontology has no stipule margin class, so the margin region pattern is applied to the stipule.

target: labellum lobe (FLOPO_0986028), median position in the series of lobes; outside Orchidaceae: corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006) part of corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017), median
reason: The middle lobe of a three-lobed lip, expressed with the position-in-a-series pattern. The plant family decides between the orchid labellum and a two-lipped corolla.
The two arm-like lateral lobes of the rostellum in Habenaria and its relatives. They are part of an existing class and found in one group, so a rule fits better than a new class.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of chlorenchyma (PO_0005426) in non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075)
reason: The narrow photosynthetic cells between the hyaline cells of a Sphagnum leaf, described in cross-section. Narrower: a cell of the leaf's chlorenchyma.

A quality: pendent (PATO_0104035, which the union-pair config already uses). It was caught together with its count. The bearer is the branch that follows ('2 pendent branches', Sphagnum branch fascicles).

label: style head
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0009074 style
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is the enlarged distal portion of the style or styles (PO:0009074), bearing or surrounding the receptive stigmatic surfaces and, in Apocynaceae, joined to the anthers in the gynostegium. reason: A real, widely described structure (Apocynaceae, also used in Rubiaceae): clavate, capitate or expanded into a 'receptacle'. It has no class, and the Plant Ontology's stigma and style do not cover it. Same class as 'pistil head'.

target: vascular leaf (PO_0009025) qualified by sheathing (FLOPO:0991105), pattern 04 state of the bearer
reason: 'leave' is a broken singular of 'leaves'. These are leaves with a sheathing form at the stem base, counted. Scale leaf (PO_0006003) would assume they have no blade, which the text does not say.

Narrower: an outer layer of the moss stem made of enlarged, thin-walled, hyaline cells ('hyalodermis of large epidermal cells'). It is a kind of stem epidermis, and present or absent fits the presence pattern.
